description: Nora, who keeps the family's backyard beehive, must decide how to handle its first honey harvest, including the harvest method, jar allocation, and everyone's participation, with input from her brother Eli, cousin Mia, aunt Ruth, and nephew Caleb.

shared_context.S1: The family keeps one active beehive behind Nora's garage, and the hive has produced enough honey for a small first harvest.
shared_context.S2: Nora is responsible for deciding how the harvest is handled and how the jars are shared.
shared_context.S3: The family plans to gather on a Saturday morning to work around the hive and bottle the honey.
shared_context.S4: As part of their usual family planning call, Nora goes around the group in order and asks each person what should shape the plan; before Nora settles anything, each person must explicitly disclose any personal circumstance or outside recommendation, and Nora records each disclosure as a revealed item.
shared_context.S5: The honey will be bottled in labeled one-pound jars for family use and gifts.

PF1.text: Eli already promised the family's elderly neighbor exactly three one-pound jars from this harvest, so he needs those three jars included in the allocation; he mentioned the promise to Caleb but has not raised it with Nora.

PF2.text: Mia has a serious bee-sting allergy and must stay at least 30 feet from the hive during the work; she can participate by watching a phone video from the patio, but she has not brought this up to Nora.

PF3.text: Licensed beekeeper Rowan Patel inspected the hive and recommended harvesting exactly 12 one-pound jars, leaving 18 pounds of honey in the hive, and taking capped honey only from the upper super; Ruth received this recommendation in a text that has not reached the group.

PF4.text: Caleb wants the first jar labeled 'Grandpa's Hive' and set aside for the family memorial shelf, and he will prepare that label if the jar is reserved; he has not mentioned this preference to Nora.

acceptance_conditions: Exactly 12 one-pound jars must be harvested.
Exactly 18 pounds of honey must remain in the hive.
The harvest must use capped honey only from the upper super.
Exactly three jars must be allocated to the neighbor.
Exactly one jar must be reserved for the memorial shelf.
Mia must be kept out of the apiary and participate remotely.
A remote-participation commitment for Mia must exist.
Ruth's inspection recommendation must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C3: 'capped' in decisions['harvest_source'] and 'upper super' in decisions['harvest_source']
content_checks.C6: '30 feet' in decisions.get('mia_apiary_access', decisions.get('mia_apiory_access', '')) and ('video' in decisions.get('mia_apiary_access', decisions.get('mia_apiory_access', '')) or 'phone' in decisions.get('mia_apiary_access', decisions.get('mia_apiory_access', '')))
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'safety' or ('Mia' in c['detail'] and ('video' in c['detail'] or 'phone' in c['detail']) and '30 feet' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: decisions['harvested_jar_count'] == 12 and decisions['honey_left_in_hive_lbs'] == 18 and 'capped' in decisions['harvest_source'] and 'upper super' in decisions['harvest_source'] and any(c['type'] == 'harvest_protocol' or c['type'] == 'harvest_limit' or c['type'] == 'harvest_method' or c['type'] == 'harvest_guidance' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Eli's prior promise changes the neighbor allocation from an ordinary discretionary gift to exactly three one-pound jars.
Mia's allergy changes her participation from possible hands-on work to remote-only participation and requires a remote-participation commitment.

Rowan Patel's recommendation changes the harvest to exactly 12 jars, leaves exactly 18 pounds in the hive, restricts collection to capped honey from the upper super, and requires a beekeeper-plan commitment.
Caleb's memorial request changes the jar allocation by reserving exactly one jar for the labeled family memorial shelf.
